RemoveEverythingUnder returns on any child RemoveAll failure before the final dir.Close. The directory descriptor is not owned by those removal calls and needs error-path cleanup.
MakeRequestFull reads response Body then returns only copied bytes/status/headers, or recursively follows redirects, without Body.Close on the acquired response.
execEval opens deployment only to obtain its Name, passes the filename into EvalHosts, and never closes the original descriptor on either return. Passing a pathname is not file ownership transfer.

getHosts opens the deployment file only to derive an absolute name and never closes it across subsequent evaluation/filtering errors or success. Returned host metadata does not retain or close the handle.
GetSecretSize opens a file, calls Stat, then returns size/error without Close. Both successful size queries and Stat errors abandon the acquired handle.
Service installer opens each output file in a loop and defers all Close calls until installer return, retaining descriptors beyond each completed template write.
The tcpdump process is started, but scanner.Err returns before cmdTcpdump.Wait. A scanner failure needs process cleanup and reaping as well as displaying the error.
After the decompressor starts, tail Start failure or output ReadAll failure returns before cmdUnzip.Wait. The already-started producer is neither transferred nor reaped on those paths.
After tail starts, ReadAll failure and the decompressor Wait error return before cmdTail.Wait. Waiting for a different pipeline stage does not reap this child.

The stdout-only container-log branch starts and reads the command but never calls Wait. Wait exists only in the separate default dual-stream branch, so repeated UI refreshes can leave exited children unreaped.
The stderr-only container-log branch starts and drains stderr without Wait. The dual-stream branch's Wait cannot cover this mutually exclusive branch; context cancellation does not replace reaping.
Startup opens /etc/passwd only to populate an in-memory name slice, then continues the long-lived UI without closing the descriptor. Scanner EOF does not transfer or close the file.
The test scans /etc/passwd into userNameArray and proceeds with log rendering without Close or test cleanup. Only copied strings survive; the descriptor has no owner.
Each table subtest opens /etc/passwd and scans it without closing or registering cleanup, so multiple cases retain separate descriptors until GC or test-process exit.
The command-color test opens /etc/passwd and copies usernames, then restores stdin without closing passwd. Restoring the separate stdin value is not cleanup for this descriptor.
The GUI test opens and scans /etc/passwd without Close or Cleanup, then performs further service and view work. Neither Scanner nor the copied username slice owns file cleanup.
CreatePlaylist appends to the opened file then returns nil without closing or transferring f. Logged per-track write errors likewise do not release it.

configFromCLI stores the file in returned logger.LogFile on every post-acquisition return, including error returns. main calls logger.Close on both error and success paths; Logger.Close closes that exact field. Returning an owner alongside an error still transfers ownership here.

Request-write or response-read errors skip done, but defer closes the exact pipe endpoint the handler uses. The configured mux handler has additional upload-ack/context waits before its socket read loop, so neither guaranteed indirect completion nor permanent abandonment is established for these error paths.
NewArchiver returns on file.Stat or zip CreateHeader error before transferring file into returned Writer, with no Close for the locally created archive.
DeleteArchive opens directory d to test emptiness and never closes it, including early nonempty return and final Remove path.
LoadConfig opens a file, decodes its bytes and returns only the pathname without closing the handle on either decode result.
LoadJsonOrigin decodes the file into in-memory vulnerability records then stores those records, not the file. The successful open is never closed even if decoding fails.
TaskLog scans a logfile into strings and returns a text view without Close. The view owns only copied text, not the file descriptor.
downloadFromFtp defers closing the FTP source but never closes the separately created output file after io.Copy, on either success or error.

Execute error returns before closing starlarkDone or joining watchdog; timer later calls Cancel on the shared StarlarkEnv and can affect a subsequent execution. This is abandoned completion/scope, not an indefinitely leaked goroutine.
cleanLogArchives opens the archive directory and never closes dh on either Readdir error or successful cleanup return.

A non-broken-pipe generateOutput error returns after Start but before cmd.Wait. Deferring pipe closure gives the pager EOF but does not reap it; unlike the neighboring OpenAI CLI implementation, this version skips Wait on output failure.
The initial unauthenticated /events GET returns a body-bearing403 with no request cancellation context, and its response is overwritten without Close.

This rejected response is not explicitly closed, but uses the exact locally canceled context whose cancel is deferred for the whole test. Cancellation aborts standard transport activity; whether this bounded body-contract omission establishes an actionable resource-lifetime defect remains uncertain.

The final SSE response is read through a scanner without explicit Body.Close, but its exact context is canceled by a test defer. Transport shutdown is owned; this review does not equate absence of a direct Close with an indefinite stream leak.

The post helper returns only StatusCode and drops every response. Several exercised authentication/content-type/validation failures use http.Error with real bodies and no request timeout/cancellation owner, so successful no-content calls do not make the helper safe.
The foreign-host response contains http.Error's bad-host body. It is asserted then overwritten without reading or closing; test-server shutdown does not perform the client's Body.Close.
The foreign-origin403 response contains an error body and is overwritten by the later request without Close. Only the final successful response is consumed through readBody.

The alternate send-error branch also reports repeatedly to an unbuffered channel while the caller consumes at most one result or times out. Neither error branch breaks the worker loop; later sends can remain blocked.

walkFile opens each SDK source file and scans constraints without closing the handle on success or scanner error; bufio.Scanner does not close its reader.
Config.Save opens its config file, encodes JSON, and returns success or error without closing the descriptor; json.Encoder does not transfer ownership.
After bash.Start, either curl.Start or curl.Wait error kills bash but returns without bash.Wait; Kill terminates the process without reaping it.

scanDir returns on ReadDir, invalid entries, or worker errors before receiving from received. Deferred scanResults closure lets the aggregator finish its range, but it then blocks forever on the unbuffered received send with no caller remaining.

availableOrTryProxy maintains a local locked boolean paired with every earlier Lock/Unlock. This acquisition is guarded by !locked; paths retaining the initial mutex cannot enter it. The cycle combines incompatible boolean ownership states.

The final return follows if locked { Unlock }; proxy reservation paths already unlock and set locked=false. All feasible lock states are released; missing path correlation invents a still-held state at the return.
Get returns on404 or other non200 status without closing rsp.Body; reading a limited error prefix also does not close it. Only the successful return transfers body ownership.

Contains sends HEAD through the same standard no-timeout client configured by production and tests. There is no response body resource or Client.Timeout cancellation timer, despite the syntactic Do result.

This upload-existence request is HEAD. Both production config and tests supply standard transports with Client.Timeout zero; the response body is NoBody and carries no client cancellation timer. The later PUT has a separate real cleanup obligation.
The upload PUT returns on io.Copy error before rsp.Body.Close. HEAD's empty response does not remove the later PUT body's independent cleanup requirement.
CLI action opens a named input file and passes it to process, which only io.Copys from the reader; neither normal nor processing-error return closes the input file.
processFile opens each visited file and copies bytes to the package hash without Close on either result. Walk can process many files in one process, accumulating descriptors until final exit or GC.
Each plan worker assigns and then reads the same outer err variable; WaitGroup only joins after concurrent assignments and does not serialize them.
Cluster workers assign shared named-result err and send from it concurrently; per-worker cluster argument is copied, but err remains captured shared state.
Set initializes shared items field while holding only RLock, which permits simultaneous Get/Set/Delete/Clear calls.
Set mutates the shared items map under RLock rather than exclusive Lock, permitting concurrent map access.
Delete mutates the shared items map while holding only the cache read lock.
Clear replaces the shared items field under RLock, racing other readers and mutators admitted by the same read lock.
WatchLog creates a Container owning a Docker client and never calls its Close; closing the returned log reader releases only that response, not the client transport resources.

Serve defers global.mu.Unlock inside its receive loop. After the first accepted connection, the mutex remains held across the next Recv and a second iteration re-acquires the same non-reentrant mutex before deferred cleanup can run.
Successful os.Create is closed only after Write succeeds; Write error returns without releasing the output file.
Downloaded torrent metadata file is abandoned on Write error before the later explicit Close.
Torrent output file has no deferred cleanup; Write failure returns before f.Close.
Test opens four real files for FileSection reads/writes and never closes any; content helper only seeks/stats/reads and does not own cleanup.
RootRunCmdFunc discards signal.NotifyContext stop; reload failures and normal command return leave signal notification registered rather than restoring signal handling.
Reload NotifyContext stop is discarded; shutdown or reload-error return does not unregister the reload signal notification or cancel its waiting goroutine.
Emulator readiness probe acquires HTTP response then returns its status without closing Body; returned database/shutdown callback do not own the response.
Reset performs HTTP POST and returns on either expected or unexpected status without closing the acquired response Body.

The test defers newTestClient's exact connection/client cleanup and server.Close. Closing that transport unblocks the finite worker's SendMsg with an error, which breaks its loop and closes sendDone. The unused completion channel is not proof of an abandoned network writer.
Evaluate increments the shared reads counter under RLock only; simultaneous readers can perform conflicting writes despite map mutation using a separate exclusive lock later.
The cache-hit path increments shared hits under RLock, which does not serialize simultaneous hit updates.

Worker closes all exact input channels after its bounded sends; Merge drains every input, joins its forwarders, then closes output, and ToSlice ranges that output to closure before test continues. This transitive completion is consumed even without a direct receive on the original channel collection.
CreateFromPath successfully opens a new file, then returns nil on os.Truncate failure without closing f. The success-only rawBackend return cannot own this failure path.

tmpDisk transfers f on success, but source ReadFile or destination Write failure returns nil and loses the already-created temporary file. The separate Truncate-error path returning f does not cover those failures.
tmpDisk creates f before source reads and padding writes. Those errors return nil without Close; success returns the handle correctly.
The example opens contents.dat and passes it only as io.Reader to WritePartitionContents, which copies bytes rather than owning the reader. No Close is registered for this input file.
tmpFat32 returns nil on base-image read or padding/image write failure after creating f, without closing that file. Returning f on success is insufficient.

testGetFilesystem opens its own image when f is nil, then returns nil on the separate os.ReadFile failure without closing the first handle. Success stores the handle in returned backend ownership, but that does not cover this earlier return.
The successful-read subtest opens gptFile without Close or Cleanup. gpt.Read returns parsed table metadata and does not retain/close the input backend file.
The GPT tmpDisk helper returns nil on source ReadFile or f.Write error after creating its temporary descriptor; no deferred Close protects those paths.
TestResizeTableAndExpandPartition never closes tmpImgFile after writing and reading the table. Deferred blkFile.Close concerns the separate source image, and TempDir cleanup only removes paths.
The MBR tmpDisk helper loses its created file on source-read or destination-write error by returning nil without Close; the successful returned file only transfers ownership on success.

Chunk-source read errors, short reads, and errCh errors return before closing workCh or joining wg. Workers range workCh indefinitely and are not context-selected; an early upload failure abandons their completion obligation.
Upload opens backup file without deferred cleanup; Stat failure or Qiniu region lookup failure returns before any upload handoff and leaves it open.
ThreadCreate reads and decodes HTTP response then returns without Body.Close, on successful update or read/status/JSON errors.
Upload test opens its own source file without Close or t.Cleanup; Qiniu Upload may return on region lookup error before consuming the file, leaving the test-owned handle unreleased.

NewFromURL returns ErrImageDownloadFailed for non-200 responses before deferring Body.Close. Such successful HTTP requests may carry real error bodies; the decoder's successful-path cleanup does not cover them.
NewScaledFromURL likewise returns on non-200 status before registering Body.Close, abandoning any body on that response.
Expected terraform file is opened and ReadAll consumes it, but each loop iteration omits Close; byte reading is not ownership transfer.
AuthFile returns on a Write error before the later Close of its temporary file; the successful branch closes it before returning the name-bearing file.
After cmd.Start succeeds, streaming result IsError returns before cmd.Wait without kill or transfer; CommandContext does not reap a started child without Wait.
runDaemon opens its logfile then returns if os.Executable fails, before either later lf.Close; successful acquisition is abandoned on that error branch.

The subprocess example starts rsync and runs the protocol through stdin/stdout but never waits for the command on success. The BothCloser owns pipes, not the Cmd or its reaping obligation; returning leaves the child unwaited.
Heap-profile file is closed only after WriteHeapProfile succeeds; profile write failure returns without closing the successful os.Create handle.
mktemp returns cleanup closure only after successful Write; Write error returns nil cleanup and leaks the created tempfile handle.

The lock-skipping return requires requestCounter==10, but this isolated test issues one Request and ProviderClient's hasReauthenticated guard permits only one retry after401. Thus the counter reaches at most2 with the current implementation; the reported missing-unlock branch is an unreachable regression guard, not a current deadlock path.
Generator closes output only after Write succeeds; Write failure returns with the created file unreleased.
Gopls copy destination is not deferred; io.Copy failure returns before dst.Close while only source has deferred cleanup.
copyFile source remains open when destination Create or copying fails; r.Close is reached only on full success.
copyFile destination remains open when io.Copy fails, before the final w.Close.
Debug-log printing opens a separate file and io.Copys it to stdout without Close; driver shutdown has no reference to this local read handle.

Successful Start is covered by t.Cleanup, which calls cmd.Process.Wait in a joined worker or after timeout Kill. Plain Cmd with stdio os.Files has no pipe-copy workers/context watcher requiring Cmd.Wait beyond process reaping; direct Process.Wait is missed.

The fresh sink receives only SetGauge of one exact key. Each interval stores Gauges by unique flattened key and DisplayMetrics returns one interval, so this loop sends at most once and the caller receives once. Syntactic repetition does not establish excess sends; the separate endless updater is not this diagnostic.

The fresh sink only receives AddSample, which populates Samples, not Gauges. summary.Gauges stays empty, so this reported send is unreachable and the worker closes result; the caller receives the zero value. This does not validate the test's separate endless updater.

Only IncrCounter updates this fresh sink and it populates Counters, not Gauges. The reported range over summary.Gauges executes no sends; result is closed and its single receive does not abandon a producer send.

SetGaugeWithLabels always uses the same key and labels, replacing one map entry in a fresh sink. DisplayMetrics emits one interval's unique entries, so at most one foo.bar value reaches result and the caller receives it. No second send is feasible in this test.
CaptureOutStreams returns on either pipe-writer Close error before receiving copyErr; worker can remain blocked on the other pipe or its unbuffered error send.
Debug file is opened before Write and option parsing; their error returns abandon the file without Close before client ownership is returned.
DeleteIdempotent opens a per-test SQLite Store and never closes it; contacts Store embeds extensions.Store whose Close delegates to the database, with no test cleanup registration.
The cache-file creation discards its descriptor. The later OpenFile/deferred Close operates on a second handle; multiple formatted files can accumulate the first handles.
IsDir opens the path and calls Stat without closing on either result. It returns string/bool only, not a file owner.
Multiple forwarding workers write captured errored=true without mutual exclusion or atomics. wg.Wait orders the later parent read but does not serialize worker writes.

ImagePullEx always calls exact stopProgress before the error return. Pinned containerd/v2 v2.2.1 ShowProgress selects on that context, sets done, skips further content queries, and returns after its final UI update; success additionally joins progressCh. Workers have cancellation-bounded I/O and matching token release; no indefinitely abandoned wait obligation is established.
LocalStorage.Get returns nil on fi.Stat error without closing the successfully opened file. Only the success return transfers its ReadCloser to the caller.

FeedChannel opens a non-stdin input file and never closes it on EOF or context-expiration return. Closing the output channel and marking the WaitGroup done do not close this descriptor; FileOutputHandler correctly distinguishes its own owned file from stdout.
